title: Autosuggest reconcile API + webhook gateway for safe batching/caching recommendations
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Optimize currently emits batching and caching recommendations but automated apply flows are fragile: retries and duplicate webhook deliveries can cause repeated or partial config changes, and there's no previewing or safe reconcile path integrated with SDKs. Goal: Ship a dedicated autosuggest reconcile API + webhook gateway that supports dry-run/preview, deterministic idempotent apply, per-change tracing, and an SDK-friendly contract for safe apply/rollback.
acceptance_criteria: API: /v1/optimize/autosuggest/apply endpoint accepts idempotency-key header and returns stable change_id immediately (100ms p50) for common cases
Dry-run: clients can request preview diffs without mutating control plane (dry_run=true), and preview contains tokenized cost delta and per-route impact estimates
Webhook gateway: a single inbound webhook endpoint that verifies signatures, converts provider retries into idempotent apply attempts, and emits ack/accept/reject events back to sender
Exactly-once semantics: identical requests (same idempotency-key or computed change_hash) must not produce duplicate effective config changes; server must dedupe within 7 days
Rollback: provide a /v1/optimize/autosuggest/rollback endpoint that accepts a change_id and reverts to previous pinned config with audit trail
SDK integration: Python and TypeScript SDKs provide helpers to compute deterministic change_hash and exponential-backoff retry helpers that use server status codes per contract
Observability: every change is traceable in Console with tokenized cost delta, applied_by, change_id, and a link to the diff artifact
DLQ for failed reconsiles: failed webhook-delivery or apply that cannot be reconciled automatically is surfaced to a per-customer DLQ and an admin can requeue via Console.
technical_notes: High-level design: accept an ApplyProposal object (target: service/route id, suggested_batch_size, suggested_cache_ttl, reason, confidence_score, preview_only flag). Server computes a deterministic change_hash = sha256(customer_id + target + normalized_patch + policy_version) and stores proposals in a proposal table with status {pending, applied, rolled_back, failed}. Apply flow: client POST -> server stores proposal and responds with change_id and current status. If preview_only, status=previewed and no downstream apply is executed. For apply flows we implement optimistic commit with a lease and use a single transactional write to the config store. To guard against concurrent/duplicate applies we require either idempotency-key header or client-supplied change_hash. We keep a per-customer dedupe index with TTL 7d. For webhooks we front with a gateway that canonicalizes provider payloads and does signature verification using shared secret+timestamp (HMAC-SHA256). Gateway transforms webhook into internal ApplyProposal and passes through same dedupe logic. Failure modes include transient infra failure (retries), semantic conflict (config drift) which triggers a reconcile flow that produces a human review ticket if auto-merge fails.
api_contract:
Primary endpoints:
- POST /v1/optimize/autosuggest/apply
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>, Idempotency-Key: <uuid or change_hash>, Content-Type: application/json
  Body (JSON): {
    "customer_id": "cus_...",
    "target": "service:chat-gen:route-16",
    "suggestions": [{"type":"batch_size","value":32},{"type":"cache_ttl","value":3600}],
    "reason": "optimize autosuggest v2",
    "preview_only": false
  }
  Success: 202 Accepted, body: {"change_id":"chg_abc123","status":"pending","preview":{"cost_delta":"-12.4%","latency_risk":"low"}}
  Errors: 409 Conflict when semantic diff applies against a newer pinned change, 422 Validation error, 401 Unauthorized.
- POST /v1/optimize/autosuggest/rollback
  Body: {"change_id":"chg_..."} -> 200 with audit link or 404 if not found
- GET /v1/optimize/autosuggest/{change_id}
  Returns full proposal record and timeline.
Idempotency: server dedup logic first checks Idempotency-Key header, then fallback to computed change_hash. If duplicate found return 200 with existing change_id. Server logs original request fingerprint and canonicalized body hash for debugging.
webhook_contract:
Inbound webhook gateway responsibilities:
- Accepts provider payloads (first-class: GitHub Actions, internal optimize-runner, marketplace connectors).
- Validate signature: X-RW-Signature: sha256=..., X-RW-Timestamp: unix_ts. Reject if |now-ts| > 5m.
- Map to ApplyProposal and compute change_hash.
- Deduplicate and enqueue apply. If apply succeeds respond 200. If accepted but processing async return 202.
- Retries: gateway treats provider retries as identical if signature+payload canonicalize to same change_hash. For non-idempotent providers we expose an ack endpoint for providers to poll: POST /v1/optimize/webhook/ack with {provider_event_id} that returns internal_change_id if known.
- DLQ: after N=5 failed attempts with exponential backoff we persist the event to per-customer DLQ and emit Console alert and Slack notification to oncall.
- Security: all webhook payloads are stored encrypted at rest and sensitive fields redacted in Console preview.
idempotency_design: Principles: deterministic change identity, short-circuit server-side dedupe, observable audit trail. Implementation details: compute change_hash = hex(sha256(canonical_json(normalize(suggestions) + customer_id + target + policy_version))). The canonical_json omits fields like preview_only and order of suggestions is normalized (sorted by type). Accept either Idempotency-Key header (prefer) or change_hash if header absent. Store (change_hash -> change_id) mapping with 7d TTL. For cross-region customers we replicate dedupe index with causal consistency for 1 minute using change vector and last-writer-wins for identical change_hash. Edge-case: two semantically different requests that collide on hash are extremely unlikely; we detect collision by comparing stored canonical request and erroring if mismatch. Rollback: rollback is implemented as a new change record with revert metadata pointing to replaced change_id so history remains immutable.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Local dev and unit tests + SDK helpers (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Internal dogfood on staging with 3 internal customers and feature flag (1 week)
Phase 2: Beta with 5 customers opt-in; monitor DLQ, dedupe hit-rate, false positives (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% of autosuggest traffic while enabling server-side dedupe TTL=7d and circuit-breaker for high failure rate (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Full rollout and postmortem + playbook update (1 week)
testing_plan: Unit tests for change_hash canonicalization and collision detection
Integration tests: provider webhook -> gateway -> apply -> confirm config store state
Chaos test: random duplicate deliveries and delayed retries to ensure idempotency dedupe works
E2E with SDK sample app to exercise Idempotency-Key retry loop and observe Console traces
Performance test: 1k/s apply requests in sandbox to validate p50 write latency < 200ms for cache hits
monitoring_alerts: DLQ growth rate > 10 events/hour for 10 minutes -> P0 alert to oncall
Dedupe hit ratio < 90% for inbound webhook events -> investigate provider churn
% of applies returning 409 Conflict > 1% -> alert and auto-disable autosuggest for affected customers
Average apply latency > 500ms for 5m window -> scale control-plane write units
rollback_plan: For semantic conflicts or failed rollouts we mark the problematic change_id as suspended and create a revert change that points to the last healthy pinned config. Admins can initiate rollback from Console which calls /autosuggest/rollback. For catastrophic failure we have a manual emergency path to pin older config and pause autosuggest agent via feature flag. All rollbacks create immutable audit entries and trigger evaluation runs to detect regressions.
security_considerations: Webhook signature verification required. Enforce least-privilege IAM for SDK tokens used to call apply endpoint (scoped to customer and maybe route-level). Rate-limit tokens to prevent abuse. All stored proposals and diffs are encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys when available. Add an audit log entry for every apply/rollback with actor, ip, user-agent. Request parsing rejects any field longer than 64KB to prevent amplification attacks.
